messages:
maria: Field squad — we need clear pilot gates for the Optimize toolkit pilot with AcmeHealth. Their main asks: batching latency p95 <= 300ms for short contexts, cache hit >= 20% on common prefixes, a quantization recommendation path (no forced auto-quant in MVP), and eval-triggered alerts for prompt/regression detection. Can we map this into an acceptance matrix?
aj: +1. We should separate MUST vs SHOULD. I'll draft an acceptance matrix this afternoon and post here.
devon: FYI AcmeHealth SLA notes: 99.9% uptime requirement and p99 latency target < 1s for their interactive flows. They care about behavior parity between Hosted and Dedicated.
sophie: Important callout — quantization can change model outputs on domain-specific prompts. We need eval-triggered alerts tied to canonical prompt sets and human review hooks.
maria: Agreed. Suggest gates: 1) Perf SLOs (p95/p99), 2) Safety/quality eval pass on core intents, 3) Rollout plan with canary (5% traffic). If an eval alert fires, we should at minimum pause rollout; post-MVP we can auto-rollback.
aj: Proposed acceptance matrix snippet:
```
Gate A: Performance baseline
  - p95 latency (short context) <= 300ms
  - p99 latency (interactive) <= 1s
Gate B: Caching effectiveness
  - cache hitrate >= 20% for top 50 routes
Gate C: Eval/quality
  - precision on core intents >= 0.95 (measured on customer vignettes)
Rollback: manual for MVP, auto-fallback to float32 model in Phase 2
```
Thoughts?
devon: Cache target 20% seems reasonable as an initial bar. Platform should expose TTL + per-route hints so field squad can tune without code changes.
sophie: For eval alerts, we should split thresholds: latency-sensitive cohorts vs quality-sensitive. Recommend alerts when absolute delta > 5% on critical-intent precision or when unknown-token rate increases by > 8%.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started on dedicated pool (canary-id: c-784) :rocket:
aj: Ops req — we need observability hooks: token-level cost, cache hitrate by route, eval alert timeline, and model-variant traces. UX can provide dashboard mocks, product-bot can create a ticket.
maria: Customer asks prioritized: 1) perf SLOs (must), 2) eval alerts (must), 3) quant recommendations (should). We should trade off advanced auto-features vs time-to-pilot.
devon: Proposal to scope MVP: batching + cache + basic quant profiles (recommend-only) + eval alerts as read-only (no auto-rollback). Post-MVP (Phase 2): auto-rollback, auto-quant suggestions, TTL auto-tuning.
sophie: Risk note: auto-quant without human review increases hallucination/regression risk. Start with recommendations that require ops sign-off.
aj: Acceptance checklist for pilot:
- Perf synthetic harness run against AcmeHealth corpus (baseline + candidate)
- Eval pass on 3 core intents (customer-provided prompt set)
- Observability: dashboards + alerting for cache/hitrate, latency, cost
- Runbook + rollback playbook documented
- Field kickoff doc and support contact
maria: Can eng commit to an MVP in 6 weeks? If not, we need to trim features or accept a phased pilot.
devon: 6 weeks is optimistic. Suggest 2-phase approach: Phase 1 (4w) = batching + cache + monitoring + canary; Phase 2 (4w) = quant recommendation UI + eval alerting + automated rollback experiments.
sophie: :thumbsup: I'll draft the eval alert rules and an example prompt set this afternoon and post in this thread.
aj: I'll update the product spec with the two-phase plan and link the playbook + UX mocks when ready.
maria: Thanks — can we review Tuesday 11am? Please bring perf numbers (p95/p99) from the synthetic harness and an initial acceptance matrix.
